subject: science
intro: The periodic table organizes the elements by increasing atomic number (the number of protons). Elements in the same column, called a group, have the same number of outer (valence) electrons, which gives them similar chemical properties. Patterns run across and down the table: metals are on the left, nonmetals on the right, and reactivity follows predictable trends. Because properties depend on the outer electrons, the table lets us predict how an element will behave.

items.prompt: Two elements are in the same column (group) of the periodic table. What can you predict about their chemical properties, and why?

steps: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer (valence) electrons.
Chemical properties depend mainly on the outer electrons.
So elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.
solution.answer: They have similar chemical properties, because they have the same number of outer electrons.

items.prompt: The periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number. What is the atomic number?

steps: Each element has a defining number on the table.
The atomic number is the number of protons in the atom.
The table lists elements in order of increasing atomic number.
solution.answer: The number of protons in the atom.

items.prompt: Sodium is a very reactive metal on the far left. What does its position suggest about how easily it reacts?

steps: Position on the table reflects electron patterns and reactivity trends.
Metals on the far left tend to lose their one outer electron easily, making them very reactive.
So sodium's position suggests it reacts easily.
solution.answer: Its far-left position suggests it reacts very easily, because such metals lose their outer electron readily.

items.prompt: What determines an element's chemical properties?

steps: Chemical behavior comes from the electrons available to interact.
It is mainly the outer (valence) electrons that determine chemical properties.

items.prompt: Elements on the right side of the table (except the last column) tend to gain electrons. How does this relate to their outer electrons?

steps: These nonmetals have nearly full outer electron levels.
They tend to gain a few electrons to fill that outer level.
So their outer-electron pattern explains why they gain electrons in reactions.
solution.answer: They have nearly full outer levels, so they tend to gain electrons to fill them.

items.prompt: Predict whether an element in the same group as chlorine would behave similarly, and explain using the table as a model.

steps: Chlorine is in a group of nonmetals that gain one electron.
An element in the same group has the same number of outer electrons as chlorine.
So it would behave similarly, also tending to gain one electron, which the table predicts.
solution.answer: Yes, it would behave similarly because it shares chlorine's number of outer electrons, so the table predicts similar behavior.
